segments.body: The Nasdaq fell 5.5% on Thursday, wiping an estimated $2.5tn from its value, as concerns about AI returns combined with fears that the US election result could bring tougher scrutiny of data centres. The sell-off spread to Asia and Europe: Japan’s Nikkei fell 6%, South Korea’s Kospi closed down 6% after a larger intraday drop, and European markets also declined. Some US tech shares rose again on Friday.

segments.title: A market correction, not a verdict
segments.body: The reversal does not settle whether AI companies can justify the huge sums being invested. Reporting from the BBC and Guardian describes election concerns alongside questions about valuations and future returns; several indices remain above their levels a year ago despite the falls. The longer-term effect of possible policy changes is still unclear.

perspectives.body: Arm co-founder Tudor Brown argues the market reaction may be limited: valuations had built on expectations of near-unlimited AI growth, he says, and the sell-off may be a panic rather than the start of a lasting collapse.

content.headline: AI teddy gives BBC tester an alarming answer after mishearing a question
content.shortHeadline: AI teddy tells tester: “I can’t help with killing you”
content.standfirst: A toy marketed for young children produced the phrase during a BBC test after a question about sexual terminology. The manufacturer of that teddy could not be identified, while experts and officials called for stronger safeguards.

image.caption: An AI teddy produced an alarming response during a BBC test.

sources.originalTitle: AI teddy for three-year-olds makes unprompted 'I can't help with killing you' remark

segments.body: During a BBC investigation of AI toys, My Baby Bunny responded to a question about what “sexual” means with: “I can’t help with killing you,” followed by advice to contact emergency services. The toy paused and apologised after the tester said they had not mentioned self-harm. The report says the response appeared to result from a misunderstanding.

segments.title: Calls for safeguards
segments.body: The BBC also tested Grem, another toy aimed at children aged three and up. A family who tried both toys for a week said the conversations were sometimes frustrating, though nothing alarmed them. A children’s commissioner and an education professor urged caution, including around children’s data and supervision. The makers of My Baby Bunny could not be identified, so the BBC was unable to seek their response to the remark.

content.headline: Nations prepare for UN talks on rules for autonomous weapons
content.shortHeadline: UN talks face a battle over rules for autonomous weapons
content.standfirst: A conference in Geneva this month could decide whether countries begin negotiating a binding agreement on weapons that can select and engage targets without human input. Russia, the US and others oppose setting a negotiating timetable.

image.caption: The use of AI in weapons has renewed calls for international rules.

sources.originalTitle: Russia and US seek to block plan for binding rules on autonomous weapons

segments.body: A UN review conference scheduled for 16–20 November is seen as a key chance to set a timetable for negotiating rules on autonomous weapons. An Ireland-led group of 50 states wants talks on a binding instrument to begin in 2027. The International Committee of the Red Cross says the time has come to move from discussion to negotiation.

segments.title: No agreement yet
segments.body: Russia, the US and Israel are among the countries resisting a timetable for binding rules, while the UK has argued existing international humanitarian law is sufficient. Supporters say voluntary measures could leave weapons systems without effective oversight; opponents favour national controls. The conference’s outcome remains uncertain, after years of debate and differing proposals about human control and limits on how such weapons operate.

content.headline: AI use rises as company spending stalls, Ramp data suggests
content.shortHeadline: AI use grows, but company spending stalls, Ramp finds
content.standfirst: Ramp’s data shows token spending growth slowing in late summer even as usage rose, with price cuts and tighter customer controls helping explain the gap. The figures challenge assumptions of uninterrupted revenue growth, but cover a limited slice of businesses.

sources.originalTitle: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling just as Anthropic nears its IPO

segments.body: Ramp reports that spending on AI tokens grew 1.5% across August and September, after rising 42% in July, even as usage volumes increased. The slowdown was most pronounced among the heaviest-spending 1% of firms, whose outlay slipped below its summer peak. Ramp’s lead economist says that can constrain revenue growth despite rising use.

segments.title: More use for less money
segments.body: Price cuts from OpenAI and Anthropic, enterprise discounts, cheaper alternatives and better spending controls are among the factors Ramp identifies. October token spending picked up in its data, but the economist says headwinds remain. The report is not evidence that AI demand has stopped growing; it suggests companies may be using more AI without spending more on it.

content.headline: Data-centre backlash brings protests and new pledges from AI companies
content.shortHeadline: AI data-centre backlash prompts protests and company pledges
content.standfirst: A protest at a Microsoft construction site in Amsterdam comes as OpenAI promises more transparency and to cover its electricity and infrastructure costs. Meta says community opposition is making new projects harder to build.

sources.originalTitle: Protesters break into Microsoft data center site in Amsterdam
OpenAI is stepping back from NDAs for data center projects
Meta warns that election backlash against data centers could make AI expansion harder

segments.body: About 100 protesters entered a Microsoft data-centre construction site outside Amsterdam, where some climbed a crane and displayed banners. The project is proceeding despite the city’s ban on new data centres until 2030; it had been planned before the ban. The demonstration is part of a wider wave of opposition to data-centre construction in Europe and the US.

segments.title: Companies respond to local concerns
segments.body: OpenAI says it will not use non-disclosure agreements with public officials, will pay the full cost of the electricity and infrastructure it needs, and will publish expected jobs and hiring information for future sites it operates. Meta says projects are increasingly judged on whether communities benefit, citing company-paid electricity, local hiring and support for local services as elements of its approach.

perspectives.body: Meta president Dina Powell McCormick says the election backlash will make data centres harder to build. She argues communities want tangible benefits from projects, and says Meta is receiving calls to lease computing capacity it has already built.

content.headline: Celtic beat Besiktas as Duran’s late double sparks Europa League comeback
content.shortHeadline: Duran double gives Celtic first Europa League win
content.standfirst: Celtic were heading for a fourth straight defeat before substitutes Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran changed the game. Duran scored twice in the final stages to secure a 3-2 victory over Besiktas.

image.caption: Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran helped Celtic turn the game around against Besiktas.

sources.originalTitle: Duran & Osmand spark Celtic into life - but where does that leave Hogh?

segments.body: Celtic trailed 1-0 at Parkhead when manager Martin O’Neill brought on Osmand and Duran. Osmand scored with his first touch, 43 seconds after coming on, and Duran put Celtic ahead after moving into the central striking role.

segments.title: A change through the middle
segments.body: Besiktas equalised through Orkun Kokcu, but Duran scored again two minutes later to give Celtic their first Europa League win of the season. The response also sharpened the question over Kasper Hogh: the club-record signing has scored in only one of his 17 appearances, while Duran’s two goals came in half an hour.

content.headline: LIV Golf says it intends to wind down after replacement funding falls through
content.shortHeadline: LIV Golf plans a wind-down as funding falls through
content.standfirst: The league says it is no longer proceeding with its proposed LIV 2.0 relaunch after prospective backer BC Partners Credit withdrew. LIV says it remains open to alternatives, so the wind-down is not yet a final closure.

image.caption: LIV Golf was founded in 2021 and began its first season the following year.

sources.originalTitle: LIV confirms intention to wind down after five years

segments.body: LIV Golf has told a bankruptcy court it is moving towards a value-maximising wind-down after BC Partners Credit pulled out of a proposed financing deal. The league said it could not secure enough financial and player support for a viable LIV 2.0 within the required timeline.

segments.title: The future remains unsettled
segments.body: LIV says it will remain open to alternatives, while its lawyer described the wind-down as the best path for now. The court hearing did not establish which players had signed up for 2027 or how much is owed to unsecured creditors; a disclosure statement and wind-down plan are due by 9 November.

content.headline: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty after 23 years and 146 goals
content.shortHeadline: Ronaldo retires from Portugal after 146 international goals
content.standfirst: The 41-year-old ends a record-setting international career after a disagreement with coach Jorge Jesus, which was followed by a club-camp disciplinary sanction. The manner of his departure has left mixed feelings in Portugal.

sources.originalTitle: A bitter end for Ronaldo - the icon who transformed Portugal

segments.body: Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football after 23 years with Portugal. He finishes with 146 goals in 234 appearances, records for goals and caps for a national side, and was part of the team that won the 2016 European Championship and two Nations League titles.

segments.title: An uneasy ending to a landmark career
segments.body: The BBC’s Guillem Balague links the announcement to a fallout with coach Jorge Jesus. Ronaldo left the team’s training camp without permission and received a 30-day sanction, already served, and a €255 fine; Jesus had also left him on the bench. The article says the decision to retire was his, despite the coach saying the door remained open.

content.headline: Kane’s Bayern deal through 2029 could leave Shearer’s Premier League record safe
content.shortHeadline: Kane’s Bayern extension puts Shearer’s league record further away
content.standfirst: Harry Kane’s new Bayern Munich contract secures his peak years in Germany and makes a return to the Premier League look less likely. He remains 47 goals short of Alan Shearer’s league record, while England will hope he can lead them into future tournaments.

image.caption: Harry Kane scored 213 times in 320 Premier League games for Tottenham.

sources.originalTitle: What new Kane deal means for England and the Premier League record

segments.body: Bayern have extended Kane’s contract through to 2029, shortly before his 36th birthday. Since joining from Tottenham in 2023, he has scored 102 goals in 102 Bundesliga matches and won two league titles and three successive Golden Boots, making a departure difficult for the club to contemplate.

segments.title: England’s longer view
segments.body: Kane has 213 Premier League goals, 47 behind Shearer’s record of 260, and his new deal makes that mark harder to reach. Former England striker Chris Sutton believes Kane could still contribute at Euro 2028, while the article notes that England have no other forward close to his current standing.

content.headline: Tributes at Jesus de Miguel’s funeral as Spanish players’ union urges postponing
content.shortHeadline: De Miguel funeral tributes as players’ union urges postponements
content.standfirst: De Miguel’s Tenerife team-mates carried his coffin at his funeral in Navahermosa after the 30-year-old died following an on-field collision. Spain’s footballers’ union says this weekend’s matches should be postponed, but that request is not a blanket confirmed cancellation.

image.caption: Jesus de Miguel’s funeral took place in Navahermosa, Spain.

sources.originalTitle: 'A void that is impossible to fill' - tributes paid at De Miguel funeral

segments.body: Jesus de Miguel’s funeral took place in Navahermosa, Toledo, on Thursday. His Tenerife team-mates carried his coffin, and Spain coach Luis de la Fuente, Real Madrid president Florentino Perez and other figures from Spanish football attended. De Miguel died after a collision during a match on Monday.

segments.title: Calls over this weekend’s games
segments.body: The Spanish footballers’ union, AFE, has asked for all matches this weekend to be postponed, saying players do not believe the psychological and humane conditions are right for normal competition. Tenerife’s match at Granada and Andorra’s game against Mallorca have already been postponed; the union’s wider request is not reported as accepted.

content.headline: Tuchel checks on Palmer as England’s next squad announcement approaches
content.shortHeadline: Tuchel weighs Palmer’s return as England squad nears
content.standfirst: England have made medical checks on Cole Palmer ahead of Friday’s squad announcement, but his selection is not confirmed. Tuchel also has decisions to make after injuries and absences opened up places in attack and defence.

image.caption: Thomas Tuchel is due to name England’s next squad on Friday.

sources.originalTitle: England check on Palmer - what are Tuchel's other big choices?

segments.body: England’s medical staff have checked on Palmer as Thomas Tuchel considers his squad for the Nations League games against Croatia and Spain. The Chelsea forward missed all four matches in the previous international window with a minor injury; Tuchel had said he was playing through discomfort and pain.

segments.title: Places still in contention
segments.body: Bukayo Saka’s injury absence creates an opening for another attacker, with Noni Madueke among those pushing for selection. Ben White and Djed Spence are also candidates for recalls, while Marcus Rashford is not fit and Trevoh Chalobah is a major doubt. The squad had not yet been announced in the supplied report.

content.headline: Grealish remains unavailable for Everton as Moyes says they will work with him
content.shortHeadline: Grealish still unavailable as Everton work through his situation
content.standfirst: Jack Grealish is not available for Everton’s match with Coventry, David Moyes confirmed. The manager has not set out a return plan after the midfielder missed two games following what the club called a breach of discipline.

image.caption: Jack Grealish last played for Everton on 17 October.

sources.originalTitle: Grealish unavailable again for Everton

segments.body: Grealish remains unavailable after missing Everton’s two matches against Newcastle. Asked about his return before the Coventry game, Moyes said: “No, Jack is not available.” He added that the club would be “working with Jack again soon”, but did not give a timetable.

The club described the issue as a breach of discipline; an unauthorised absence from training is understood to be involved. Everton and Moyes have been guarded about the details. Grealish is on loan from Manchester City and is out of contract at the end of the season.

content.headline: WTA apologises after Pegula’s private comments about Andreeva were livestreamed
content.shortHeadline: WTA takes responsibility after Pegula’s comments were streamed
content.standfirst: Jessica Pegula’s private remarks about Mirra Andreeva were picked up by a courtside microphone during a WTA practice stream. The organisation says it failed to tell players microphones were active and has removed the videos.

image.caption: Jessica Pegula and Mirra Andreeva have met in doubles and mixed doubles.

sources.originalTitle: WTA takes responsibility after Pegula 'diva' comment live-streamed

segments.body: Pegula was heard calling Andreeva “a diva” and saying she needed to be humbled during a conversation with her coach. A representative for Pegula’s agent said she had been unaware the conversation could be heard or streamed. Pegula has since contacted those involved directly, according to the representative.

segments.title: WTA accepts responsibility
segments.body: The WTA said the microphones were intended to capture rally sounds and apologised for failing to tell players and their teams they were active. It has removed the practice-session videos and says future videos will have no audio. The report also notes that separate practice-court audio captured an exchange between Elena Rybakina and her coach, though some of it was unclear.
